handoff.purpose: Define _CumulativeGateCancelled exception and implement _promote_one_inner with staleness handling, retry, git apply, commit, and cancellable command_gate.

symbols.name: _CumulativeGateCancelled
symbols.note: Exception raised when cumulative gate is cancelled; inherits from RuntimeError.

symbols.name: _promote_one_inner
symbols.note: Promotes a single candidate: handles staleness, git apply, commit, and optionally runs test command via command_gate.

claims.text: The cumulative re-gate stopped because ``cancel`` fired, not because a test genuinely failed.
claims.why: The chunk defines the exception but does not show where it is caught or how cancel firing leads to it; the logic in _promote_one_inner raises it on gate_result.cancelled, confirming the claim in that context.

claims.text: Raised (never silently swallowed) so the SAME fabricated-verdict shape this repo already fixed once -- a cooperative stop reported as an ordinary gate failure -- cannot recur here
claims.why: The chunk does not show the except block that catches this exception; the swallowing behavior is not visible.

claims.text: the ``except`` block below still resets the integration worktree exactly as it does for a real failure (that reset is unconditional and was already safe for cancellation before this class existed
claims.why: The except block is not fully shown in this chunk (starts at line 797 but ends abruptly); reset behavior is not visible.

claims.text: the REASON string a caller sees now says ``cancelled``, not ``gate failed``
claims.why: In _promote_one_inner, when gate_result.cancelled is true, the exception is raised with message starting 'cumulative gate cancelled after ...'.

claims.text: STALENESS. Every candidate after the first, in the normal case of 2+ writes gated concurrently against one shared starting commit, WILL have artifact.base_revision != current_head the moment it is this candidate's turn -- that inequality is not an edge case here, it is the expected shape.
claims.why: The code checks artifact.base_revision != current_head and handles it as expected, not as an error.

claims.text: A `git apply --check` passing would only prove the bytes still match; it says nothing about whether the change is still semantically correct now that an earlier candidate has landed ahead of it. So: regenerate against the current integration state instead of trusting a check.
claims.why: The code does not use git apply --check; instead it regenerates via _reattempt when base_revision differs.

claims.text: Bounded to ONE retry -- a second staleness hit means something is landing candidates faster than this one can be recomputed, which is a reason to stop and report, not to loop.
claims.why: The code checks _retried flag; if True and base moved again, it returns with reason about second regeneration refusal.

claims.text: NOTHING WRITTEN. `git apply` (no --3way, no --reject) validates the whole patch before writing anything; a non-zero exit here means the integration worktree is exactly as it was before this call. Refused and reported, never retried with a fuzzier match and never merged with conflict markers.
claims.why: The code uses git.run with check=False and returns on non-zero returncode without further retry or fuzziness.

claims.text: cumulative re-gate needs test_cwd='.'; project configures {test_cwd!r}
claims.why: The code raises RuntimeError if test_cwd not in (None, '', '.'), stating the requirement.

claims.text: WAS `lambda: False` (uncancellable) -- this is the one gate in the promote path that runs the project's WHOLE test command, so it is the longest-running thing a stop request can land inside. Safe to make cancellable: the `except` block just below already resets the integration worktree to `current_head` unconditionally on ANY failure here, cancellation included, so honouring `cancel` adds no new way to leave that worktree in a worse state than finishing would -- it only shortens how long a stop takes to land.
claims.why: The except block is not fully shown; reset behavior is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: Distinct exception type on purpose -- see _CumulativeGateCancelled's own docstring: the reason string a caller reads back must say 'cancelled', never 'gate failed', or this reintroduces the exact fabricated-verdict shape this parameter exists to close.
claims.why: The code raises _CumulativeGateCancelled with message starting 'cumulative gate cancelled after ...' instead of 'gate failed'.
